rows.note: For ordinary physical departure or telling someone to go away, 走 is the all-purpose choice; in context it can also mean quitting a group or organization.

example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 jiu3 zau2 laa3

rows.note: Use 放 when you put or leave an object somewhere, especially when it is to remain there or be collected later.

example.english: I’ll leave the documents at the reception desk; you can pick them up later.
example.traditional: 我放份文件喺前台，你得閒自己攞。
example.jyutping: ngo5 fong3 fan6 man4 gin6 hai2 cin4 toi4 nei5 dak1 haan4 zi6 gei2 lo2

rows.note: Use 留 when you leave something behind or keep some of it remaining instead of taking or using it all.

example.english: If you can’t finish it, leave some for me.
example.traditional: 你食唔晒就留返啲畀我。
example.jyutping: nei5 sik6 m4 saai3 zau6 lau4 faan1 di1 bei2 ngo5

rows.note: Use 由得 when you leave someone free to act or leave a matter for someone else to handle without interfering.

example.english: Leave this matter to them to handle themselves.
example.traditional: 呢件事由得佢哋自己搞啦。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 jau4 dak1 keoi5 dei6 zi6 gei2 gaau2 laa1
